item.title: The Invisible Half of a Career: Financial Literacy
item.description:
This post is part of my “Before Choosing a Career” series on career choice and planning. All posts in the series: Career

When it comes to choosing a profession, a topic that isn’t talked about much in Turkey also comes into play: financial literacy. In my opinion, children and young people need to learn this at an early age.

Note: I am sharing my own thoughts in this post. I am not a financial advisor, and this post is not investment advice.

item.title: Example: What Working in IT Is Really Like
item.description:
This article is part of my “Before Choosing a Career” series on career planning and choosing a profession. All parts of the series: Career

In the previous part, I mentioned that when evaluating a profession, you need to look at how a day, a week, or a month actually unfolds in that role. Here, I want to give an example from my own field: IT.

My goal is to help those who are just starting out or considering stepping into this field visualize what things actually look like. Putting myself in their shoes, I remember there were many topics I couldn’t grasp simply because I didn’t know what some of the terms meant. That’s why I’ll also try to briefly explain the terminology.

item.title: The Myth of a Single Profession: You Can Have Multiple Careers Throughout Life
item.description:
This post is part of the “Before Choosing a Career” series I prepared on career choice and planning. All parts of the series: Career

People often hold the belief: “I will choose one profession, make my living from it, and all my income will come from this single job.” In reality, that is not entirely true.

We don’t have to stick to just one profession throughout our lives. We can acquire multiple professions and work more than one job at the same time.

item.title: Write Down Your Goals, Work a Little Every Day
item.description:
This post is part of the “Before Choosing a Career” series I prepared on career choice and career planning. All parts of the series: Career

Those who want to switch careers, recent graduates, university students… Let’s say you’ve decided on the profession you want to pursue. From this point on, you need to establish a working routine.

Instead of hiding behind excuses like “I’m so busy right now, I have so much work, I’m too tired,” you need to get things done, even if it’s just a little bit every day.

item.title: Career Research with AI: A Step-by-Step Plan
item.description:
This post is part of my “Before Choosing a Career” series on career choice and planning. All posts in the series: Career

My advice to young people on this topic is this: Gather information using today’s AI tools. But instead of just telling these tools “I want this,” conduct real research with them.

Use deep research mode
#

When doing research, be sure to use deep research and web browsing features. This feature scours numerous sources across the internet and compiles a comprehensive report for you. It’s usually limited—often to something like once per day on free tiers. That’s why breaking your research down across several days makes a lot of sense.
